executiveSummary: GM0575 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 45,929-person municipality control, 44 neighbourhoods in six districts, three BAG places, eight BRT settlement labels, 81 scheduled-transit stop areas, zero conventional rail stations and five NWB logical links are coherent; rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 45,955, only 26 above the separately published control (+0.057%). Release is nevertheless correction-required. Noordwijk has 13 km of North Sea beach and robust dunes, a primary coastal-defence pathway, distinct Rijnland polder/boezem/sewer/groundwater mechanisms, intensively used dune and forest areas, and seasonal population that VRHM says doubles from March through October. The coastal preset emits exactly 2.317791 m at T+6 through T+24, 21,317 affected resident-equivalents and 482,380.705 deprived person-hours at T+24 without selecting a sea/wave boundary, current defence state, breach/overtopping variant, LIWO Noordwijk footprint, arrival, duration or recession. It then makes direct water exactly zero at T+48 and calls T+72 recovering even though the official extreme coastal scenario says water can move deep into the region within hours and repairs may not begin for weeks to months. The major-river preset likewise fixes 0.437295 m from T+12 through T+72 without a selected Lek/IJssel, Rijnland-boezem or regional-defence connection. The canonical remote wildfire produces zero direct flame, while a controlled ignition inside Buitengebied Noordwijk Noord produces 0.460175 flame but ranks its source neighbourhood 30th of 44. Resident-led allocation puts inland Zeeburg first for the coastal case and the same seven areas lead eight unrelated active presets, omitting the municipality's beach, visitor, care, dune, access and water-control geography. Public records identify 35 water objects, a Dunea river-to-dune drinking-water dependency, one electricity-planning sample, 85 antennas, 28 education locations and no acute-care point inside the boundary, but these are context rather than live topology, capacity or restoration. Unknown, NoData, catalogue no-match and static register status must never become zero, open, safe or operational.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0575 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region data
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0575 as Noordwijk in Zuid-Holland and Hollands-Midden and report 45,929 residents, density 787/km², 23.7% aged 65 or older and 8,049 one-person households; the generated centre [4.466920615403533,52.26272934855237] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Forty-four neighbourhood rows in six districts sum to 45,955 residents, 26 above the separately rounded municipality control (+0.057%); households sum to 21,120 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 10,875. Model allocation reconciles to the control without rewriting observations.

BAG supplies De Zilk, Noordwijk and Noordwijkerhout; BRT supplies three woonkernen, two deelkernen, two gehuchten and one buurtschap: De Klei, De Zilk, Noordwijk, Noordwijk aan Zee, Noordwijk-Binnen, Noordwijkerhout, Ruigenhoek and Sancta Maria.

CBS regional statistics expose 36 fields. District heating and public charging are null in all 44 rows; cars per household is null in five, housing-value/tenure fields in three, benefit fields in two and doctor/supermarket/density fields in one. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0; null/suppression remains NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Noordwijk municipality risk profile and regional risk-profile appendix
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal profile; regional profile appendix published for the current VRHM risk-profile site, with source references mainly 2021–2022
supports: VRHM describes 13 km of sandy beach and robust dunes, bulb fields, woods, recreation parks, hotels and hospitality. It states that population doubles from March through October and remains high on weekends; these are planning/activity indicators, not incident-time occupancy.

The profile says the sea defence was strengthened in 2007–2008 and a dike and wider dunes protect Noordwijk and the region. It lists floods, nature fire, extreme weather and interruption of electricity, gas, drinking water, wastewater, telecom and food among relevant risks; inclusion is eligibility, not a current event.

The regional appendix says primary-defence failure is most plausible around Katwijk, Noordwijk and Westland because dunes are narrow, despite strengthening, and requires a very severe northwesterly storm with very high sea level. Its extreme coast case has multiple failures and seawater moving deep into the region within hours.

The appendix distinguishes first indications around eight days, sufficiently accurate coastal water/wave expectations around two days and continued local breach uncertainty to the event. Impact depends on breach count/size, water height/duration, hinterland, defence and roads; repair may not start for weeks to months and complete recovery may take years. No standard reuse licence or machine cadence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — LIWO 2025.1.6 Noordwijk primary-breach candidate and Waterinfo point context
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO application 2025.1.6; public WFS queried 3 September 2026; Waterinfo snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: The bounded public LIWO WFS returns primary candidate 2161 named Noordwijk at [4.4517,52.2610], inside GM0575. Catalogue frequency flags are metadata for scenario selection, not an active failure, probability forecast, connected inundation footprint or local depth.

LIWO is versioned professional scenario information requiring water-manager interpretation. A causal use must pin release, scenario/model dates, source water, sea/wave boundary and datum, defence/breach/overtopping variant, depth/velocity/arrival/duration/recession grids, native resolution/CRS/units, uncertainty, coverage, NoData, licence and approval.

No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is assigned inside GM0575 in the deployment snapshots. The nearest observation is IJGeul at 22.64 km and the nearest forecast point is Scheveningen at 22.88 km; points outside the municipality are not local wave, defence or inland-depth evidence.

Waterinfo observations are generally ten-minute CC0 public/non-mission-critical context; the rolling CC0 forecast cache has declining horizon coverage and no water-level features at requested T+72. No local match or empty horizon is NoData, never zero water or safe state.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Rijnland coast, Hogeveensepolder and public water-control/wastewater context
evidenceSources.edition: Hogeveensepolder design decision 2026; Rijnland strand rules/planning current in 2026; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Rijnland says the Hogeveensepolder in Noordwijk and Lisse is largely bulb fields and generally meets the water-nuisance norm, but recorded levels differ from formally adopted levels since pumps were installed, level-area boundaries differ from practice and excessive intake causes flushing. A new level area and formal decision are in progress in 2026.

Current Rijnland coastal policy says space is needed for dune growth and works with a long-term two-metre sea-level-rise allowance; beach buildings can obstruct growth and phased seaward movement is expected from 2026. This is long-term planning, not current defence condition or incident forcing.

Full-boundary assignment in the HWH deployment snapshot finds 35 points: 32 surface-water pumps, two DWA/RWA sewer pumps and AWZI Noordwijk. The register is national, contributor-dependent/partial, weekly for IMWA where supplied and CC BY-SA 4.0; status 'gerealiseerd' is registered existence, not operating state.

Some public capacities are numeric and many are null, with unverified register units. Points do not establish compatible hydraulic topology, catchments, level areas, sea/boezem constraints, telemetry, power/backup, live condition, overflow, water quality or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Waterafvoerverordening, crisis communication and first-72-hour household guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Waterafvoerverordening valid from 29 August 2024; current municipal crisis and emergency-kit pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The valid Noordwijk water-discharge ordinance distinguishes wastewater, stormwater and groundwater systems, requires 60 mm parcel storage in covered cases and calls for water-on-street calculations that include sewer and surface runoff. It is a design/rule baseline, not live capacity or a municipality-wide depth grid.

The municipality tells households to prepare for the first 72 hours, including three litres of water per person per day, food, radio, power bank, medication and a ready evacuation bag. This is public preparedness advice, not evidence that households possess supplies.

Current crisis guidance uses NL-Alert, municipal channels, Hollands Midden Veilig and TV/Radio West as the regional emergency broadcaster. It does not publish exercised local support points, evacuation/shelter zones, resources, staffing, care capacity, route clearance or restoration commitments.

The municipal pages and official regulation are publicly viewable; no standard machine API, reuse licence or incident cadence was identified. Planning requirements and generic instructions must remain separate from event-authorised actions and verification.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Noordwijk drinking-water service area and river–dune supply dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Drinkwatervoorziening van de toekomst 2030–2040 planning document; current Berkheide programme inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Dunea identifies Noordwijk inside its northern service area, primarily supplied through Berkheide at Katwijk. The system depends on pretreated river water from the Afgedamde Maas, with the Lek as an alternate source, transported to coastal dunes for infiltration and subsequent treatment.

Dunea says long transport distances, pipe breaks and source contamination can threaten continuous supply. The current Berkheide programme includes an Overbrugging Katwijk project for temporary deep-groundwater use when river-water transport is interrupted.

Berkheide is both drinking-water infrastructure and protected/recreational dune landscape; current works say Winning 3 produces about 7.3 billion litres annually and is being renovated. These planning/design figures do not establish incident flow, storage, quality, redundancy, accessibility or operating state.

Public operator documents expose functional dependencies but not sensitive physical distribution topology, live telemetry, outage, backup endurance or restoration. No standard redistribution licence or stable machine incident feed was identified during this audit.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Zuid-Holland / ProRail / OVapi / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — NWB and N206 access, scheduled transit, rail and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; current Province N206 page; GTFS version 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB graph gives five mobility/supply-only boundary links: N206 toward Katwijk and Bloemendaal, N444 and N443 toward Teylingen and N442 toward Hillegom. The two N206 records are one physical corridor and their nominal 150 scenario-units are non-additive, not measured emergency capacity.

The Province describes the N206 as a regional route from Zoetermeer through Leiden and Katwijk to Aerdenhout. Static geometry/project information does not establish live passability, direction, closure, evacuation function or access to the A4/A44 network.

No conventional ProRail station lies inside GM0575. OVapi GTFS version 9543 assigns 81 stop areas, including beach, dunes, recreation, Groot Hoogwaak, Space Expo and Willem van den Bergh locations; schedule and stop geometry do not establish passengers, accessibility, vehicles or emergency service.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 assigns no emergency department inside GM0575; LUMC in Leiden is nearest at 10.76 km straight-line and reports a 24/7 ED. Questionnaire status is dated context, not travel time, acceptance, occupancy, staffing, generator endurance or guaranteed capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM / KNMI
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Electricity planning, communications, education, air-quality and weather observations
supports: One NBNL postcode sample at 2211XT maps to Liander OS NOORDWIJK 10-1i and reports planning values of 22/23 MW existing/required withdrawal, a 1.2 MW nine-request withdrawal queue, 22/12 MW injection and a 9 MW injection queue with request count null. At-least-quarterly/monthly planning is not full coverage, live load, outage, switching or reserve; the product is described as open data but an exact licence identifier was not found.

RDI assigns 85 antenna installations: 41 mobile, 18 fixed-link, 20 amateur, one broadcast and five other-mobile. Its WFS states no reuse licence or cadence. DUO daily attribution-licensed RIO data assigns 28 education locations: fifteen primary, two secondary, three special and eight other registered uses.

One Luchtmeetnet station inside the municipality, De Zilk-Vogelaarsdreef, observed indicative PM2.5 3.38 µg/m³ at 17:00Z on 2 September 2026. The hourly public service states no standard reuse licence; a point observation is not a municipal smoke surface, source attribution or scenario forecast.

No KNMI observation station lies inside GM0575; Nieuw-Vennep is nearest at 12.34 km and its cached 23:30Z record has null temperature and hourly-rain values. KNMI observations are ten-minute CC BY 4.0 context and must not be projected through synthetic T+72 or interpreted as zero where fields are absent.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Noordwijk dune-fire risk and current regional nature-fire phase semantics
evidenceSources.edition: Current daily regional phase inspected 3 September 2026; VRHM Noordwijk RIN context dated 2017 in the regional profile
supports: VRHM's Noordwijk dune Risk Index for Nature Fire identifies care institutions, intensive recreation, limited primary/secondary firefighting water and poor emergency-service access; it notes first-vehicle arrival can exceed fifteen minutes in nature areas. This is official risk context, not an ignition or perimeter.

The national Brandweer page showed Hollands Midden Phase 1 at access time. It explains that the phase is reviewed daily using regional measurements, KNMI information, field expertise and observation and may be changed around midnight.

A regional daily phase describes potential for fire spread and public precautions; it is not a local fuel/moisture raster, ignition, forecast, incident perimeter, smoke plume or suppression-resource state and must never automatically drive a canonical event without clock alignment.

The page is public operational communication but no standard reuse licence or stable machine API is stated. Local exercise integration requires authority approval, provenance and controlled disclosure of responder-access information.

The model has no watch/warning, evacuation/shelter, rescue, dewatering, route, care, supply, inspection or re-entry ledger.

findings.summary: The named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset emits persistent direct water without a selected local hydraulic route.

VRHM describes possible regional consequences from Lek/IJssel failure, but the simulator selects no source hydrograph, defence, connected footprint or relationship to Rijnland boezem/polders.
findings.action: Suppress exact direct river depth and dependent effects until a water manager selects a connected major-river/regional-defence case. Keep North Sea, Lek/IJssel, boezem/polder, pluvial/sewer and groundwater mechanisms separately typed; no selected route is Unknown, not safe.

Static design/register values remain non-causal.

CBS residents, including official zero Klei-Oost, are the only people control; 81 stop areas show visitor/care destinations but do not measure occupancy. findings.action: Add authoritative dated occupancy bands for beach zones, accommodation/recreation, care, education, events and employment, separately from residents. Preserve time/season, coverage, uncertainty and licence; never infer people directly from stops, businesses, buildings or annual totals.

residualLimitations: This is an audit of a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a KNMI/WMCN/VRHM warning, hydraulic forecast, evacuation order, outage statement, route guarantee, casualty estimate or operator restoration commitment.
CBS 2025 neighbourhood figures are rounded/suppressed and need not sum exactly to the municipality control; allocation reconciliation does not rewrite the published 26-person difference.
The generalized administrative boundary cannot represent sea, beach, dunes, primary defence, polders/level areas, groundwater, buildings, catchments or exact hazard intersections.
LIWO candidate 2161 is a catalogue point, not an active breach, probability, connected footprint, forecast or local depth; selected-layer reuse terms and expert approval remain required.
VRHM's extreme coast case is an official scenario, not a prediction that Noordwijk's strengthened 2007–2008 defence has failed or that one municipality-wide depth applies.
No local Waterinfo/KNMI point and empty T+72 forecast coverage are scoped NoData. External station values cannot establish Noordwijk waves, defence state, rainfall, flood depth or canonical T+0.
Hogeveensepolder's norm compliance is planning/assessment context, not an all-weather guarantee; its real/formal level differences and 2026 decision process require versioning.

The 35 HWH points have contributor-dependent completeness and do not establish connected topology, compatible register units, telemetry, power/backup, live state, overflow, water quality or restoration.
Dunea public planning documents identify functional source/transport/dune dependencies but not sensitive topology, current storage/quality/flow, outage, redundancy, backup endurance or restoration.
NWB, Province pages, GTFS, RIVM, NBNL, RDI and DUO data do not establish live passability, passengers, occupancy, acceptance, physical utility topology, coverage, capacity, backup or repair.
Registered residents omit seasonal beach, hotel, park, event, care and worker presence; VRHM's seasonal doubling and static site counts are not incident-time occupancy.
The daily Hollands Midden nature-fire phase is timestamped regional potential, not a local source, fuel raster, perimeter, smoke forecast, access or suppression state.
The single De Zilk indicative air-quality observation is not a continuous exposure surface, source attribution, smoke plume or forecast and its public service states no standard reuse licence.

Official zero residents, zero canonical direct fire, zero post-event depth and zero model ground motion are narrow source/model statements, not proof of zero activity, risk, damage, water, seismicity or indirect effects.
Support-point locations, shelter roles/capacity, household preparedness, care acceptance, mutual aid, staffing, crews, fuel, stocks, dewatering and recovery beyond T+72 remain unverified.
